subject: Staggered GPU onboarding playbook for EdgeScale renewal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam@edgescale.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Staggered GPU onboarding playbook for EdgeScale renewal

Hi Sam — great to meet last week. As we discussed on the call, your Q2 usage patterns show sharp peaks around model training windows and a steady baseline for inference. To make the renewal low-friction and keep your unit costs predictable, I sketched a staggered ("staircase") onboarding approach that lets you add capacity in controlled tranches rather than one big commit.

Quick asks to make the plan prescriptive:
- Can you share a 30/60/90-day rolling token and job trace (we usually accept CSV or a compressed snapshot) so we can align burst windows to tranche sizes?
- Any hard SLA or latency SLO requirements for the busiest routes?

I attached a short template you can drop data into — if you send the CSV I can populate the cost estimates and propose a concrete three-tranche commit with fallback rules.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send the usage CSV (30/60/90).
2) Redwood runs a quick sizing + simulation and proposes two tranche mixes (balanced vs. conservative).
3) Align on rollout cadence (30 days apart recommended) and observability gates to trigger the next tranche.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: staircase-sizing-playbook.pdf (PDF stub), EdgeScale_usage_May2026.csv (template stub)

From: Sam Carter <sam@edgescale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staggered GPU onboarding playbook for EdgeScale renewal

Jordan — attaching a compressed snapshot of May usage. See high-level notes below and a public link to our internal runbook.

Notes:
- Peak windows: weekdays 09:30–11:00 and 15:30–17:00 PST, driven by batch model retrains.
- Baseline inference is ~35% of peak sustained.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for <4k token prompts.
- We're open to a staged commit; primary ask is a predictable cost floor for budgeting.

I attached: usage_snapshot_may.zip (contains token-level traces), plus our internal procurement timeline (we're aiming to sign by 2026-06-10).

—Sam
Sam Carter
Head of ML Ops, EdgeScale Systems
Attachments: usage_snapshot_may.zip (ZIP stub)
Related link: https://edgescale.internal/runbooks/retrain-schedule (internal)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam@edgescale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staggered GPU onboarding playbook for EdgeScale renewal

Thanks Sam — got the snapshot and timeline, helpful. I ran a quick simulation with two candidate tranche structures and attached the populated cost-estimate-tranche.csv and the Staircase playbook PDF with observability gates called out. Summary (high level):

Option A — Balanced (recommended):
- Tranche 1: +24 A100-equivalent GPUs (covers baseline + 1.1x peak headroom)
- Tranche 2 (30 days): +16 GPUs (scales to sustained peak)
- Tranche 3 (60 days): +8 GPUs (safety buffer & seasonal headroom)
- Autoscale policy: keep pre-warmed slots at 70% of tranche capacity, dynamic burst to spare pool.
- Expected blended unit cost: $X.XX/token (see CSV).

Option B — Conservative: smaller initial commit and larger final tranche (lower near-term spend but higher operational risk during peak).

Observability gates (must pass to trigger next tranche):
- 10-day rolling utilization >= 82% during identified peak windows AND
- 95th latency drift >15% vs baseline OR sustained queueing events >5% of requests for 48 hours.

Operational notes:
- We'll pin model variants for Tranche 1 to a 4-bit quantized profile for non-critical routes to lower GPU memory pressure; heavier models will run on the new dedicated pool.
- We recommend a single-canary A/B cutover for route migration to avoid double billing issues.

I've flagged two lines in the CSV where committed vs. forecasted spend diverges significantly — Ben, can you review the autoscale thresholds and confirm feasibility on our end?

Next step: if EdgeScale prefers Option A, we'll prepare an amendment that defines tranche dates, observability gates, and a DocuSign-ready commitment. Target to have that signed by 2026-06-10 to match your procurement window.

Jordan

Attachments: cost-estimate-tranche.csv (CSV stub), staircase-sizing-playbook.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staggered GPU onboarding playbook for EdgeScale renewal

Quick technical check — notes for Jordan/Sam: 
- Autoscale: the pre-warmed 70% is fine, but set burst cooldown to 15 minutes to avoid oscillation with retrain spikes.
- KV cache reclaim: recommend 12% aggressive eviction for Tranche 1 while we observe memory pressure.
- Fallback routing: add an explicit fallback to our cheaper L2 region if latency SLOs are breached for >30 minutes; this avoids customer-facing errors while we trigger tranche 2.

Also, will add a short runbook section on measuring the 10-day rolling utilization metric so there’s no ambiguity in the gate.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Carter <sam@edgescale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staggered GPU onboarding playbook for EdgeScale renewal

Jordan — this looks good. We prefer Option A (balanced). A few clarifications before we sign:
1) Can you include a short clause that defines the "safety buffer" tranche as optional but accessible within 14 days of gate pass (we occasionally need faster runway).
2) Confirm that pre-warmed slot usage will be billed at tiered discounted rates once Tranche 2 is live.
3) Send the DocuSign amendment and we'll route it through procurement; target signature by 2026-06-10.

If you can fold Ben's cooldown + eviction guidance into the amendment runbook, we're happy to proceed.

Best — Sam
Attachments: (none)
